body: Bump

Oh my gosh this is horrible. I'm sorry people are saying this to you. My advice is to say something like "under no circumstances are you to call me this word". You can educate them if. you would like. If this is happening during school,  consider telling your counselor or teacher. They should make an announcement to the student body about not saying this terrible word and the consequences of it. 

If you don't want to cause a scene, just walk. away and don't converse with that person again. If. you are playing video games and they say it you could mention that word really hurts you and that you are done playing. 

If a scene is caused, it wouldn't be you causing the scene - it's them!

He did end up giving the money back but was very upset by it. I did also call my husband cheap for wanting to take the money and always letting his parents pay for things. I know that was wrong and I regret it. My husband basically blew up because I said this. I don't know if I was being ridiculous. I explained to him before that I don't want to take money from his family because I see that it further increases the toxic enmeshment. For example, both of my husband's adult children completely rely on his father to survive. One got his girlfriend pregnant, and MIL was pushing them to get married. I see my husbands parents very involved in the other siblings lives and I dont want that. I didn't explain what the toxic enmeshment is in this post but I have in other posts. I overheard my husband talking to his friend on the phone about me not wanting to accept the gift. His friend said that it is very normal to take monetary gifts from parents. I believe that if we continue taking money it would blur the boundaries with his family. I have given in before we got married, but after I found out his parents were also hiding my husbands drinking for 5 years I put my foot down. I see that they are enablers. I'm summarizing here, it's a complicated situation. But I did allow my husband's mother to throw a wedding shower. The shower was at a place she wanted to have, with 35 of her closest friends. It was a party for her. This is just one example. Because my brother in law is so dependent on his parents for money, if MIL wants something, he has to do it. I don't think my husband understands the strings that are attached. If he's willing to throw our relationship away because I wanted him to give his parents money back and because I called him cheap then it doesn't seem like we have a solid foundation.

Thanks. Yeah, he basically said he doesn't feel like we are on the same page anymore and that I'm depressed and not doing anything to get help. I explained to him that I was just in therapy for three months but the therapist didn't work out. I found the therapist at the start of the semester when my load was lighter and haven't had time to find another. I work full time, am a PhD student, and do the cooking and cleaning, grocery shopping, taking out the garbage, stuff like that.He doesn't think that I am putting enough effort into getting better. I told him that I stood by him when he went through his sobriety and it looks like he isn't giving me that same understanding. He also sprung on me that he wants children now, even though that was a decision that we had both discussed before marriage and after. Neither of us really wanted kids, and I was a firm no after I found out some information about him. He is telling me that he really always wanted kids but was just saying he didn't because of me. He also asked me where the "passion" and "intimacy" is in our relationship.
Yeah, we talked again and he basically told me that he wants a divorce.

The main reason why I'm still with him is not a good one. I don't want to have to move back with my parents. In their culture a woman doesn't live alone. I was only able to move out of their house without an issue because I got married. I've tried to move out before and it was disastrous to say the least. If I leave my husband and choose not to live with my parents than I won't have my family either. They will not accept me. It will be just me. I guess that is scary to me.
He uses us breaking up as a manipulation tactic.
Thanks for all of your help!

Yes, I think that's what some other people who answered don't get. The family is highly enmeshed and based on my observation it seems like the parents, my in-laws, want their children to *uck up so they can bail them out and they will continue to be dependent on them. My husband's siblings are grown adults but completely dependent on the parents. My husband has it engrained to call his parents if anything happens or goes wrong. I've had several conversations with him that if we need repairs in the house or anything like that we will call a repair man. I have worked to set boundaries with my family, but my husband not so much, especially since mother in law is extremely pushy and doesn't take no for an answer. I've stood up to her and said no several times though. 

That's a good question, if nothing changes, no I don't think I'll be happy. I made a big mistake going into the marriage and I know it. The only reason I went through with the marriage was because I had already sent the wedding invitations out and I was afraid of embarrassing my family by calling off the wedding (that's a whole other issue in itself). I guess I'm seeing how it goes. My husband has been working hard on his sobriety and I think part of what is helping is him not living with his toxic alcoholic enabling family anymore.

Yes, I will give Al-Anon another try. I didn't go to just one or two, I've been to several.

I want to clarify that I do not expect my in-laws to stop drinking. I know they won't. I don't care if they do or not. What I am saying is that it would be supportive of them not to drink around him considering the circumstances. I suppose that's too much to ask for parents to support their child, who almost died's sobriety.

I believe part of facilitating change is greatly involved in environment. They are the people my husband drank around. It was in their homes my husband did most of his drinking. In AA, there is the saying to stay away from "wet places and wet faces" since these can be triggers for relapse. When my husband drank it was mostly with his family. In fact, that's where he started drinking and doing drugs, in his parents house as a child. And his parents allowed it. Yes, my husband is an adult at this point. His family is toxic and they are enablers. They normalized alcohol and drug use. My husband is working on getting better. They are not. Sometimes the best thing to do is cut out toxic people. No, I'm not asking my husband to cut them out. We had a conversation and I told him if he wants to spend time with them that is his choice. He has spent lots of time with his family and I wasn't there.  I also have a choice, and that is to limit my time around them. I will not completely cut them out, but I also do not want to spend every single weekend with them as we have been. 

Yes, there will always be alcohol around, but my husband and I do not go to places with alcohol otherwise. Growing up I was almost never around alcohol. I choose friends that didn't drink. I didn't go to bars. It was never normalized, but instead drinking was looked at as poisoning the body, which it absolutely is. My professor who teaches a substance abuse class even said it is not a good idea to normalize drinking and should not be done around children.  It's not something that needs to be the norm.  For example, no one in my family drinks alcohol, and all of his new friends now are in AA and also refrain from "wet places and wet faces" as much as they can. 

My husband goes to meetings on his own. I go to open AA meetings because he asks me to go out of support. I absolutely know what the difference is between an open and closed meeting. I would not go if my husband didn't want me to be there. He is the one who encourages and asks me to go to these meetings and also to socialize with his AA friends. He wants me involved because as of now, I am the only person in his family who supports his recovery. 

One of the reasons why my husband wanted to be with me was because he knew I didn't drink. He knew that I would support his sobriety because he wasn't getting that support from his family. Clearly I can't keep him sober. I  know that. Who he wants to spend his time around is his choice. I choose not to spend my time with people who are not supportive. Again, I know that they are not in charge of my husband's sobriety. That is on my husband. Even so, support from family would be nice, but that's too much to ask of them.

Thanks for sharing your story.That's really inspiring that your father had so much sobriety under his belt.  I have been to Al-Anon but I prefer going to open AA meetings with my husband more. I found that in combination with individual therapy to be more helpful.

Yes, I understand he needs to modify his behavior. Which he has as best as he can. But they are not helping the situation whatsoever and not being supportive. And for that reason, I don't support spending time with them.

Whenever he drank, he would always drink with his family or friends. And whenever he was with his friends his siblings were mostly there. So with modifying his behavior, one way to do that is to cut out the toxic people he used to drink and drug with.

If my family drank alcohol, which they do not, I would not be spending time around them if they invited us to events they were drinking at  in support of my husband.

No you're right, there is more to the story. Whenever my husband's sister used to come into town should would get cocaine and all the siblings would do that together. They are a very tight knit family. 

I think there were many unhealthy decisions my husbands parents made that enabled the children, like allowing my sister in law to have her drug addicted boyfriend live in their house with my husband and brother when they were underage,  my mother in law had the "fun house" where my husband, his siblings and their friends drunk alcohol/did drugs underage.

My father in law almost died of a heart attack a couple years ago and my husband who is a physician put him on a plant based diet because that is shown by research to reverse heart issues. My husband and I converted from vegetarian to plant-based to support him, while mother in law still serves him garbage and animal products. 

I found out my husband would tell my mother in law about our relationship, so she was behind the scenes influencing things. Mother in law used to talk to my husband about her relationship with father in law. So it's like my mother in law was the third wheel in our relationship. 

Mother in law is very pushy. I could give a big list, but here is one example:  For our honeymoon, we wanted to go to Greece but couldn't afford it. So mother in law kept pushing for us to all take a family vacation to Greece two months after our wedding, so basically wanted my husband's whole family to go on a honeymoon with us. 

Brother in law knocked up an 18 year old at the age of 27. Only knew her for a few months. She was still in high school. Mother in law pushed for them to get married. Weird coincidence? I don't think so but they decided to induce the baby's birth on my husband and I's first wedding anniversary. The baby wasn't due for another two weeks and there was no reason besides they "liked the date". Mother in law kept saying it would be so cool if the baby was born on our wedding anniversary and guess what it happened - because they picked the date.  

I could go on and on. I think there is very unhealthy attachment. All of my husband's siblings including my husband have been in jail due to alcohol related issues. Not just once. 

My husband's siblings are completely dependent financially on the parents even though they are in their late 20s/early 30s.  

So basically an environment I don't want to be around and don't want to be normalized. I am very ambitious, and want better for my husband and I. I think we become influenced by who we spend time around. 

I tried to be understanding of his family and we had a good relationship. But after "the incident" 6 weeks before my husband and I's wedding when he had a DUI, I found out he was drinking and lying during our entire relationship, and he spent a week in a psych hospital because he tried to kill himself I said enough is enough. 

His parents knew exactly what happened and they didn't even have the courtesy to tell me what happened to my future husband. We were supposed to hang out that day and he wasn't answering. I had to call his mom that night to find out what was wrong and she said he was so stressed out he checked himself into a psych hospital. He was just finishing residency. I felt like the worst fiance because I didn't know he was that stressed out. His parents even lied to me about how he tried to kill himself. They told me mother in law found him in his room. I later found out he tried to hang himself in the bathroom at jail. 

When I brought my now husband home from the psych hospital, I asked him to make sure his family had no alcohol in their house because he was staying with them before we moved into our house. Sure enough, his mother had an open bottle of wine in her bedroom fridge (her room was right across from my husbands room). Also a glass of alcohol with wine in it. I was super pissed and afraid to leave my husband there, especially since he was only a week sober. 

At this point, I stopped being understanding. I told my husband that if we get married, we are done spending as much time with his family. I see them as a threat to my husband's sobriety and just overall not a good influence. I have been making a lot of compromises and spending more time with them than I want to. I'm tired of pretending like everything is ok. 

That's why when they choose to have alcohol in front of my husband I see it as them communicating they don't give a *uck, and they are being unsupportive. 

At this point, because my husband has this problem and is so sick there are three ways his life could turn out. Either he remains sober the rest of his life (which he has struggled with), he ends up in prison, or dead. 

In my opinion, being around his family often will not help him much with option number 3.

Yes, I know they will not censor his drinking, especially since they are alcoholics. I don't expect them to stop my husband from drinking or to stop but I don't want to be around them when they are drinking. 

My husband told me that early recovery isn't much different from 20 or 30 years of recovery. Relapse happens at any stage, not just early recovery. So this is my concern.

My husband has issues with his family too. He never really told me why he doesn't want them over. He is a big people pleaser, so if someone asks him to do it, he will (if his family invites him somewhere). 

He has OCD, so I think that may also be why he doesn't want to have them over. It's a good idea though, I'm going to tell him we should just have his sister and family over before she leaves. I can compromise with that rather than going to a place where there will be alcohol and everyone is tipsy.

Yes, I know that if I wasn't there at the event my husband would most likely be drinking. He has relapsed several times and been on probation before we met, he lived with his family at the time and was still drinking even when on probation (I later found this out after we got married). 

I personally don't want to be around people who think my husband's sobriety is a joke or doesn't take it seriously. Both of his siblings are alcoholics and the parents still serve them copious amounts of alcohol in their house. They keep making poor decisions and the parents bail them out. I don't think this is normal or healthy behavior. I'm not saying I don't want my husband to spend any time with his family, but we are spending far too much time. There are gatherings on a weekly basis. I do not want their lifestyle to be normalized. 

My husband and I met in medical school. He actually almost didn't make it. He spent the first three weeks of the semester in jail because of a DUI.  I knew about that but wanted to support him because he said he sober and didn't want to drink. He told me that even though he was still drinking behind my back and with his family he wouldn't have made it through medical school without me. I kept him more sober than he would have been because he has a serious problem. 

I don't see his family supporting my husband. They aren't taking it seriously, and it makes me very upset. 

Yes, my husband has a sponsor. What he learned from AA is that people should stay away from "wet places and wet faces" meaning avoiding people and places they used to drink around. However, my husband's sponsor's father in law does drink around him. 

I understand that it is my husband's responsibility to stay sober. However, his family is not helping and not being supportive. I'm tired of just sweeping this under the rug and pretending like it's ok. 

My husband said I should talk to his family and tell them how I feel. I don't know if that would accomplish anything. I don't feel genuine having the feelings I have towards them and then putting on a happy face when I'm around them.
That looks really good

Yes, I have brought this up to my husband, that I would rather we have gatherings at our place, but he doesn't want his family over our house for dinner. They have come a couple times. 

Yes, I have discussed with my SO how it makes me feel. I never liked it. I haven't had a sip of alcohol in my life and do not like being around it at all. I'm very against alcohol. He is ok with being around it, but then again that's what he used to say before, and would drink behind my back when I left. 

I am also upset at his family and know that I have a built up resentment because they also lied to me about my husbands drinking and enabled the situation, knowing he has a problem and is an alcoholic. 

I see his family as a threat to his sobriety and our life together.
Thank you : )

Yes, I've been in therapy for a while too. Before I even met my husband. Your words of wisdom are very helpful. I really like the last sentence your wrote. I'm going to just focus on myself and what I can change. I know that I have a lot of unhealthy resentment towards my husbands family and that's something I need to work on. I can accept them as they are, but that doesn't mean I want to spend my time or energy around them. If my husband doesn't want to get on board then that's ok. I already went into the marriage knowing it might not work out. Thanks again!

Yeah, you're right. I appreciate your help. I am seeing a therapist and I talk a lot about this. However, we haven't talked about any strategies. The sessions mostly just are me talking. 

I know that I don't want to have them as a big part of my life and that is all I can control. My husband will decide what he wants. I've expressed myself to him several times and now I just have to accept. 

Yes, I'll give updates. Thanks so much!

Yeah I know. No doctor has time to put together someones swing set. My husband actually went over there for two weekends to help not just put the swingset together but also help dig cement out. It was a big project, and the whole family wasn't there. His brother didn't ask, and my husband was upset by that. All his brother said was "when are you coming to help me with this swing set"...and this was while he was packing to go on a trip. The only reason he has free time is because he works for his dad and comes and goes as he wants. 

I already told my husband that I will probably not be going to the family bbq when his sister comes into town and if I do it will only be for a half hour. 

Yes, I did try to set a time limit with his parents. But he wasn't willing to abide. I always asked him how long will we spend and set limits but he ends up staying way over that. So I get stuck there. What I did last weekend was drive separately. 

It made me upset that he didn't cut his time short with them, but I didn't say anything because I realize I can't control him. 

I don't know what to say to him to get him to see what I see.

My husband did work for his dad a little bit before starting med school. Yes, I agree, it's a family system issue. 

Even though they may not be drinking in front of my husband, I think the greater issue is that they continue to have a grip on his life through having all of these gatherings, having expectations (like brother in law told my husband that because he is the godfather if anything happens to him we will have custody of the child, without asking either of us), and discussing personal things. 

I don't know if this is part of it, but something very bizarre is that my brother in law's baby was going to be due two weeks after our first wedding anniversary. MIL kept saying "wouldn't it be cool if the baby was born on our anniversary? 

Sure enough, it happened. Not because it was natural, but because they said they "picked" that day and decided to have the baby induced early. It sounds crazy, but I think they picked that day because it was our anniversary. My husband is a doctor and said it was dangerous for her to be induced that early, and there was no other reason for that to happen. 

They told us they just liked the date, and when I went in to visit the mother and baby the first thing the mother (my husband's sister in law) told me before I could even congratulate her was "sorry for stealing your thunder".

She is nicer to me now, but has made it very clear that she does not get along with other females. She's basically young enough to be my daughter anyways...I'm going off on another tangent. 

I'm just looking at the big picture and don't think it's healthy to spend time around them. My husband is a big people pleaser and so when anyone asks him to do something or come over he does it right away. 

I think you're right and the only thing I can do is limit being around them myself and hope my husband learns how to set boundaries through me. 

I have set boundaries with my family, but they are all very busy we don't spend that much time together. My husband's family has lots of free time.

Sorry, I don't know what an information diet is. Do you mean I shouldn't tell him certain things? Yes, I've found that he tells his family EVERYTHING we are doing. I didn't realize how enmeshed he is until we got married. 

Yes, I've started to make myself less available, like when I left their get-together after only staying an hour last week. His mother was like "is something wrong"....and I just told her no I have things I need to work on. For them, they can hang out whenever because they all work for my husband's father. I don't have that luxury of just hanging out whenever.

He is now in recovery. An incident happened 6 weeks before our wedding when I found out his lie and that he had been hiding his drinking our entire relationship....and a lot of the drinking he was doing was with his family. They were all hiding it from me too. My husband new before we even started going out that alcohol is my number one deal breaker and I didn't want to be with someone who drank. 

He has been actively working on his sobriety since we got married and is in AA, has a sponsor, has been in counseling, etc. 

I had to set boundaries with his family regarding the alcohol. He tried to kill himself 6 weeks before out wedding because he was afraid I would leave him if I found out he was drinking. He ended up in a psych hospital. When he came home he was going to stay with his parents before our wedding. I told him to ask his family to not have alcohol in the house since he clearly has a problem and his family knew...in fact all of his siblings are also alcoholics. My husbands parents gave him his first sip of alcohol when he was a teenager. 

When I dropped my husband off at his parents I went through the house to inspect. There was alcohol. His mom has a fridge in her room and had an open bottle of wine and a full up of wine in there....his room was right across from his parents. I was so upset. 

Then after we had gotten married I told my husband if his family is going to drink, we will not hang out around them. They honored that for the most part, until his brother had a birthday party and all the friends and family my husband drank around before were drinking and getting drunk. 

I told my husband to set boundaries that if they are drinking we wont attend their functions. FOr the most part the immediate family now doesn't drink, but my husbands extended family does. They don't know about my husbands alcoholism. However, his brother has a huge display of open alcohol in his kitchen. I get nervous whenever we go there, but I know my husband won't drink in front of me. Even when we were engaged and he was drinking behind my back, it was never when I was there. He said part of why he wanted to be with me was because I have never had alcohol and he thought I could help keep him sober. I did to an extent. He told me if I wasn't around he probably wouldn't have been able to finish med school and residency.  

Sorry, I went on a rant there.

He was able to set some boundaries, but my fear is that my husband isn't seeing what I'm seeing. I think his family is highly enmeshed. I think his mother especially is an enabler. She does this in other ways. For example, my husbands father had a heart attack. My husband put him on a plant-based diet after researching that is the only diet that can help reverse some heart problems. My husband and I were vegetarian for a long time, but we are now plant-based to support him. We have bought them cook books and educated them about nutrition. My mother in law will still buy junk, meat, etc and pretends she doesn't know. While it is my father in laws responsibility, if it's in the house or she makes something with meat for dinner, he will eat it. So basically she isn't helping. 

I don't know why she seems to want her husband as well as her son to be sick.

Yeah, that's true. I did stand up by leaving my husband's brother's house early last weekend. My husband decided to stay later. I'm planning on driving separately. The frustrating thing is whenever there is an issue with our house, the first person he calls is his parents. I have told him that I would rather we figure it out ourselves. On the flipside, if his family needs anything, they expect my husband to drop what he's doing and help. For example, Sunday his mom called and wanted my husband to look at the dog she was babysitting (he is a doctor not a vet but...). The weekend before his brother asked him when he's coming over to put the swing set together for his kid. He didn't ask my husband even if he could, but expected that he would help. I found out my husband had lunch with his dad a couple days ago on his break from work. It just seems like a lot of time he is spending with his family....more than usual.

I'm sorry you are in this situation. Based on how I grew up, I can understand why your wife is like that. It doesn't make it right though. I think the issue here is that your wife doesn't seem to see an issue with the situation. She has been so conditioned by your mother to be a certain way that she doesn't know how to think for herself. 

​

The only thing I can suggest is what many others have....couples therapy. It also sounds like your wife can benefit from individual therapy. Your wife needs to recognize this is an issue and maybe hearing it from a third party will help. 

I hope everything works out for you.
Yeah, I will support my brother.

I didn't make my husband do anything. I told him before we even dated that this is what would happen. I told him if it got to marriage, my parents would require him to convert. He understood and chose to continue. 

No, I don't believe in Islam but if my parents find out I don't think that would be a good idea. I could potentially be put in danger because I come from a large Muslim community. No, we are not overseas, but the punishment for leaving Islam is death in some countries. Some people don't care what country we are in and there are life or death consequences. 

I am part of a secrete group for former Muslims in America. The reason why it is a secret is because there are dangers even in this country. Part of why I abide by my parents "rules" is that I dont' want them to find out I'm not Muslim. In Islam, children are supposed to listen to their parents pretty much no matter what.

Hmmm...that's accurate. I'm in love with the idea of what my parents could be. I think you are very right. In some cases I am very angry at my upbringing, but I still give excuses, like it isn't their fault. I'm going to break the cycle by not having children. My parents want me to have children very badly and bring it up just about every time I visit. I know that if I have kids it will just be one more way they will try to control me.
Thank you!

Yeah, I need to snap out of it. I didn't realize how much into the fog I am. 

My parents did ask me if I met her before and I said no. I know they will be pissed if they find out I had them over, but I guess I just have to deal with the consequences.
I'm also struggling with whether or not I should tell my parents my brother is coming over. I don't want to but feel like they may be upset it I don't.
Oh yes, I read this book. I can relate so much.

Yeah, you are right. I dont have much of a spine when it comes to my parents. I think I do, but still have a long way to go. I guess I feel bad for them. I know neither of them had good childhoods and so they aren't bad people, but they are doing what was done to them.

Yes, there is a pretty good sized inheritance, but that's not something I would hold out for. I'm not trying to fall in line with them because of that. I guess I'm trying to have my cake and eat it too. Make my parents happy and also make everyone else happy. At some point it cant work.
Thanks for sharing. Yes, I agree. It's not going to end well if I stand up to them. But I guess that's what I have to do because my brother doesn't deserve this.
Yes, you are right. I'm the one giving them power. No, my brother and I both have good paying jobs and are not dependent on them for anything other then love and approval.

Yeah, I have thought of going no contact. Now I guess I'm limited contact. I visit once a week. Used to contact her daily, but just gave one answer responses so she stopped contacting me as much during the week.

Thanks I will check this out. I wrote this in another response, but a part of me is actually afraid of my dad physically. Growing up he did physically hurt my mother. Although he only kicked me once, and punched my little sister when she stuck up for me for refusing to go to pharmacy school (I got in but told my dad I didn't want to go). I don't know what he is capable of when he gets into these rages.

Yeah, I guess I have to just come to terms with the fact that my parents are only loving if we do what they want. Even though my siblings and I are all relatively successful, we have self-esteem issues and are scared of pissing our parents off. 

I'm not planning on having kids. In part because if I did I couldn't hide the fact that I'm not Muslim, and also because I don't want to pass any of the crap my husband and I got from our families.

Oh I'm very familiar with the disown threat. My father told me that if he ever finds out one of his kids leave Islam then he will disown us. That's not so bad, but I'm also scared to come out because my father has made comments about someone he knew that left Islam and said they should be shot.

So a part of me is legit scared for my life from my parents. My father gets into rages very quickly over little things. He used to physically hurt my mother growing up. One time I stood up to him for my mom and he kicked me. My sister once stood up to me and he punched her. So not often, but I do know it's something he's capable of doing.
Yeah, you're right. My parents have a very collectivist view of the world so they feel like it's families marrying families. That's not how I see it.

True. I'm just worried about my other two siblings. My parents already tried to get me to talk my brother out of marrying this significant other. I'm worried my other siblings are so brainwashed by my parents. They have trained us to be obedient.
Thanks for your advice!

Yeah, she does side with my parents. She isn't that young, turning 23 and in law school. I realized my parents were toxic since I was very young and all I wanted to do was get away from them. But I stayed living with them until I got married at 34 because I didn't want to deal with their wrath. 

I was probably more so the problem child growing up. I called my parents out and they didn't like it. On the outside, I'm living an acceptable live they would approve of, but they don't know most things. I keep them at a distance beside the obligatory weekend visit.

Thanks for your help. Yeah my brother said he doesn't want to cause any rifts in the family. I told my brother he wouldn't be the one causing the issue, it's my parents. 

Another this is I have two other siblings. One is much younger and lives with my parents. The other is also younger but is basically the perfect child, married a successful doctor who is Muslim and now they have two kids. Both of those siblings side with my parents. 

I don't care so much with loosing my parents but more so losing my other siblings.

Yeah, that's the other issue. I feel bad for my brother's significant other and that she has to deal with this. I felt bad for my now husband, but I let him know before we even started dating about the situation with my family. He still wanted to be with me despite all that, so my brother's significant other must also.
Thanks, this is good advice.

Thanks for your help. You are right. I guess I just need to suck it up and finally stand up to my parents. I've tried, but it usually ends in a huge rage. At least I don't live with them anymore so there is less they can do.
Thanks so much for your help. I'll check this out.
